svg.aria-label: Call Authorization Score tiers and outcomes
svg.text: Call Authorization Score (CAS) — Tier Thresholds
CAS is a 0.0–1.0 composite score; the band it falls in determines the call's outcome.
CAS ≥ 0.90 — Verified Trust (L2)
Full access at the agent's granted scope. Highest-confidence band — typically a cryptographically
verified NHID-Auth v2 passport plus a clean v1.3 behavioral trace.
CAS ≥ 0.75 — Conditional Trust (L1)
Access granted with reduced scope or added monitoring. Strong but not perfect signal —
e.g. valid identity with a minor behavioral flag, or vice versa.
CAS ≥ 0.50 — Review Required
No automatic grant or denial. Routed to human review or a step-up challenge before the
requested action proceeds.
CAS ≥ 0.20 — Denied / Degraded
Default-deny for the requested scope; a narrower, lower-risk fallback action may still be offered.
Logged as a near-miss for trend monitoring.
CAS < 0.20 — Hard Denial
Call rejected outright with a typed error code. Written to the FHIR AuditEvent trail regardless
of outcome — denials are audited exactly as thoroughly as approvals.
Inputs to the score (src/nhid_cas.py)
v1.3 behavioral conformance (IDG-01/PDX-01/DBC-01/EIT-01) blended with, where present,
v2 cryptographic identity verification (passport validity, NPI binding, scope, nonce match).
Reference implementation: src/nhid_cas.py · 38 dedicated tests · thresholds tunable per deployment
